page: Microsoft Azure D48pls_v5 is an ARM-based compute instance powered by an Ampere Altra processor featuring 48 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture running at 3.0 GHz. Each virtual CPU corresponds directly to a single physical core without simultaneous multithreading. The system includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware acceleration for AES cryptographic operations. It is provisioned with 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. No local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs are bundled with this configuration, relying on remote Azure Premium Storage for persistent disk I/O.

Benchmark evaluation highlights robust performance in highly parallel, CPU-bound workloads. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the instance achieved a top-quartile score of 84,952.55, and demonstrated strong compiler throughput in Geekbench Clang compilation with a score of 39,161.0. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect the lower single-core IPC characteristic of the Neoverse-N1 architecture, evidenced by a weak Geekbench single-core score of 1,084.0 and bottom-quartile bzip3 single-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput align within typical median boundaries, reaching 160.48 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 36.62 GB/sec in static web tests.

The 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation creates an efficient compute profile for horizontally scaled systems, container build farms, and CI/CD automation pipelines where thread density takes priority over per-core memory capacity. The absence of local scratch disks requires architectural consideration for external storage performance, but the dedicated core mapping eliminates thread contention, making it suitable for distributed web servers, microservice clusters, and batch compilation workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D48pls_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine equipped with 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. Designed with a 1:2 memory ratio, the instance provides 96.0 GB of RAM alongside 32 MB of L3 cache, with no local ephemeral storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmarks indicate superior scaling in multi-threaded environments, posting strong results in multi-core stress testing and software compilation via Clang. Single-core performance falls into lower percentiles, marking a clear engineering tradeoff between single-thread responsiveness and dense parallel throughput. Operating via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance avoids multithreading contention by assigning each vCPU to an isolated hardware core. The D48pls_v5 is appropriate for continuous integration pipelines, batch code compilation, container clusters, and distributed microservices requiring sustained multi-core compute density.
